name: … the data: every route point with its elevation, distance from the start as in the waypoint list (lines one after another), the whole route on the horizontal axis; min / max from the file; the ascent = climb() of the elevations

… the chart: the curve through all 37 points from the left to the right edge of the plot, the highest point at the top of the data; the vertical axis at least 100 m (a flat route doesn't look like mountains) with labels in m, the horizontal one in km from 0 to the end of the route (no trailing zeros)
climb(): an ascent counts only after the elevation rises at least 3 m from the last low point (a descent likewise), then in full up to the top; values that are not numbers are skipped
… the route planner counts its climb with the same function, separately for runs of found segments (no elevation jump across a segment without a path)
A long route (6000 points, about 66 km, one 400 m spike): at most the lowest and highest point of each pixel column are drawn, the spike and the lowest point are kept
An edit redraws the profile at once (a route point 400 m high), Undo brings it back
✕ hides the profile: the map takes its place (Leaflet knows the new size), the menu item unticked, the choice stored; a toast is then above the bottom edge of the map

name: Cursor (cycle 88): the mouse over the chart shows a vertical line, a dot on the curve and the values (the distance from the start as in the waypoint list, the elevation, the grade over 50 m before and after); a mark on the map at that place of the route; nothing pinned, the map doesn't move
… near the right edge the values are on the left of the line, inside the chart; at the start the distance in metres; the mouse leaving the chart removes the cursor and the mark
A click pins the place and moves the map onto it at the same zoom; it stays after the mouse leaves; hovering elsewhere shows that place, leaving goes back to the pinned one
… the pinned place goes away with a click on the map (no waypoint added), Esc, an edit of the route

Touch: a finger moving over the chart without touching it first does nothing; dragging a finger along it moves the cursor and the mark (the map stays); lifting it pins the place and moves the map there
… a narrower window keeps the pinned place at its distance
… hiding the profile removes the cursor and the mark; shown again, nothing is pinned
